label: T2.7-parked - wire, world and deltas green; the scene does not read as the game the spec describes (no Lighting configured at all) and a player spawns 917 studs from their own dome. Multi-client contention and cross-server persistence remain UNTESTABLE.

phases.name: sync-provenance
phases.detail: 3 mounts, 46 scripts, 0 mismatches against the rojo read API. FALSIFIED FIRST: renaming ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Net produced mismatchCount=2 (both halves — MISSING ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Net and UNDECLARED ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Net_FALSIFY), label 'T2.7-unrun (hybrid or unverified place)', reachedScreenshots=false. The mutation was inverted, not checked out. The T2 harness (ServerScriptService.T2Smoke) was removed before this walk — default.project.json does not declare it, and a hybrid place cannot green this rung.

phases.name: boot-console
phases.detail: NEGATIVE: zero engine errors across boot + probes. Warnings are the 14 expected per-action B2-security notices plus the monetization-unconfigured notice (7 inert catalog entries, asset id 0 — a real handoff item, not a defect). POSITIVE (STEP 4b): the discovered marker '[JoinRetry]' MUST appear, and did, 8 times — plot.fetch, salvage.fetch, daily.claim, structures.fetch, leaderboard.fetch, depth.fetch, offline.peek, resurface.fetch each re-issued after the data push. That is the client join race being caught live; it is the defect that cost a previous game its offline earnings permanently, and a silent console here would have been indistinguishable from a missing guard.

phases.name: server-authority
phases.detail: capture-S / act / capture-S' over the REAL wire, with the delta read from a DIFFERENT service than the one that acted. structures.fetch quoted cost 91, affordable=true; after structures.buy{key='drones'}: Credits 334 -> 243 (exactly -91, the server-derived price), drones level 2 -> 3, and the income rate REPORTED BY salvage.fetch 1.5 -> 2.0 (+0.5). One CoreEvents 'data' push observed carrying 9 persisted view keys: boostExpiresUnix, currencies, daily, flags, plot, resurfaces, smelter, stats, upgrades. This is the written-never-read discipline satisfied — the purchase's effect is visible to a second service and to the persisted projection, not merely present in the reply of the call that caused it.

phases.name: client-wire
phases.detail: All 14 actions in Net.Actions invoked through ReplicatedStorage.CoreGateway FROM THE CLIENT DATAMODEL — the only rung in the factory that crosses the replication boundary. Set-diff clean: 14 declared, 14 exercised, 0 without a payload. ZERO RateLimited and ZERO UnknownAction (either would mean the request never reached its handler, i.e. unverified rather than verified-and-refused), and zero throws. Replies: plot.fetch/salvage.fetch/salvage.collect/structures.fetch/structures.buy/depth.fetch/offline.peek/offline.claim/resurface.fetch/leaderboard.fetch = ok; plot.claim = AlreadyClaimed; daily.claim = OnCooldown; depth.descend and resurface.do = PrereqUnmet. Every refusal is the handler's own documented gate, never Internal. offline.claim returning ok is the feature whose four adversarial findings were fixed today (8a434ab, c98e538, 3ce04fc, d7ad232) paying out end-to-end over the real wire.

phases.name: world-present
phases.detail: Workspace holds 658 descendants, 145 non-character BaseParts, across DeepReachPlots (314 descendants — the 60-dome ring) and DeepReachTrenches (20). Bounds 1856 x 931 x 1833 studs. A real character spawned and was standing at (-4.99, 3.06, 0.63); the single SpawnLocation is at (0, 0.5, 0). ENUMERATED by class rather than named, so a missing builder shows up as a count and not as an assertion nobody wrote: Part=142, Model=67, Folder=65, Vector3Value=69, PointLight=63, Attachment=53, StringValue=35, NumberValue=18, MeshPart=15, SurfaceGui=1, TextLabel=1. Non-zero by a wide margin — the vacuity that let a whole world's assertions pass against zero parts is not present.

phases.name: screens
phases.detail: Five shots, each with its assertion stated BEFORE the capture. Three pass (hud-play, overhead, hud-after-clip - the last VERIFIED the HUD fix, which the rect probe could not see), one FAILS (spawn-eye: the scene does not read as abyssal), one is cannot-tell (zone-dome1: legible as greybox, which v1 declares it is). Files could not be written to disk from this bridge.

findings.summary: The HUD's side panels overflow their own frames and collide with other panels' text on any viewport shorter than ~820px.
findings.measured: At viewport 1220x455, RightPanel is 292x204 (its height is 0.45 scale) while its shop list needs ~369px: rows spill up to 165px past the panel, and TopRight's depth readout spills up to 138px. Six pairs of EFFECTIVELY-visible text from different panels overlap by more than 8px in both axes — 'Hull Plating . Lv 0' x 'STORE' (264x17), '400 Credits' x 'HIDE SHOP' (264x18), 'DEPTH 1 . x1' x '243 Credits . 0 Pearls' (276x16), and three more. Confirmed visually in the overhead capture: the STORE and HIDE SHOP buttons are drawn on top of the Pearl Drone and Hull Plating rows.
findings.why: Every panel is scale-sized against viewport height, the rows are fixed-height, ClipsDescendants is false and there is no ScrollingFrame — so the layout does not degrade, it overlaps. Threshold: RightPanel = 0.45 * H must hold ~369px of rows, so it overflows below H ~= 820. A 1080p client is fine; a 720p or windowed client is not, and windowed play is common.
findings.confound-stated: The session's viewport was 1220x455 (aspect 2.68), unusually short, which exaggerates it. The threshold above is what makes this a finding rather than an artifact of one window: it is a statement about viewport HEIGHT, and it is arithmetic, not an impression.
findings.correction: An earlier sweep of this reported 7 overlaps including modal-vs-modal collisions. That was a PROBE ERROR: Roblox's GuiObject.Visible is per-instance and not computed down the tree, so labels inside StorePanel and ResurfaceConfirm (both Visible=false) were counted as visible. Re-run with an effective-visibility walk up the parent chain, exactly one modal is visible and the real count is 6 — all of them between panels that are genuinely on screen.
findings.status: PARTIALLY FIXED in this session — HudRoot now builds every slot frame with ClipsDescendants = true, guarded by a falsified source-level regression case in hudroot.spec (flipping the literal to false takes it RED; ensure() cannot run under Lune because Instance is nil, which is why the assertion is on the source).
findings.verified-how: In-engine, and NOT by the probe that found it. The rect sweep still reports 6 overlaps after the fix, because ClipsDescendants changes RENDERING while AbsolutePosition/AbsoluteSize keep reporting unclipped geometry — the instrument that found the defect is blind to its repair. The screenshot is what settled it: before, STORE and HIDE SHOP were drawn on top of the Hull Plating and Pearl Drone rows and DEPTH 1 x1 bled across the structures list; after, the structures panel truncates cleanly at Smelter Tank and both buttons sit legible below it, with no text drawn over any other text.
findings.residual: The CAUSE is unchanged: content is still taller than its slot below ~820px of viewport height, and now truncates instead of colliding. Visible cost, stated rather than glossed — TopRight's badges (DEPTH 1 x1, NEXT 1500 Cr hull 2, rich wreck depth 5, no boost active, no passes owned) are clipped away entirely at 455px of height, so that status is unreadable rather than unreachable. Truncation beats collision (the player can read what remains, and can resize), and at >=1000px neither occurs. Letting a taller-than-its-slot catalog SCROLL is a per-controller affordance and is the named follow-up; it was not attempted here.

findings.summary: The game configures NO Lighting at all, so an abyssal deep-sea trench renders as a bright afternoon sky over a flat plate.
findings.measured: Lighting is stock Roblox default in every value that matters: ClockTime 14.5, Brightness 3, Ambient and OutdoorAmbient 0.275 grey, FogColor light grey, and FogStart 0 / FogEnd 100000 - i.e. fog is effectively OFF. Its children (Sky, SunRays, Atmosphere, Bloom, DepthOfField) are the set Studio puts in every new place, not game-authored instances. Confirmed in two captures.
findings.why: The spec's Theme & tone is explicit - 'Quiet, high-pressure, industrial-deep-sea. Bioluminescent accents against dark water.' Nothing in src/ ever touches Lighting, so none of that exists at runtime. Same class as the invisible-night-sky precedent this rung was built on: correct in code, wrong in a picture.
findings.alreadyFlagged: The reachability gate has been WARNing exactly this the whole time - 'no Lighting anywhere in the tree - nothing configures the lighting the whole game is seen through' - as a non-blocking presentation WARN. It was right, and it went unread until a screenshot made it undeniable. That is an argument about the WARN tier, not about the gate.
findings.notFixedAndWhy: Deliberately NOT fixed. This is unbuilt scope - a theme feature the spec describes and no slice built - not a defect in built code, and building a lighting system unasked would widen the scope of an autonomous run. Surfaced for a decision instead.

findings.summary: A player spawns ~917 studs from the plot the join hook just claimed for them, with no observed teleport.
findings.measured: MEASURED IN THE LIVE PLAY SESSION, not inferred: the character stood at (-4.99, 3.06, 0.63) while plot.fetch reported its claimed dome_1 at x=916.73. Nearest dome to the SpawnLocation at (0, 0.5, 0) is dome_1 at 917 studs. Trench1 by contrast is 4 studs from spawn, so the depth structure IS underfoot - it is specifically the player plot that is far away.
findings.why: The dome ring has radius ~917 and spawn is at the origin. The HUD says DOME 1 / your dome / secured on frame 1 while the dome itself is a dot on the horizon, so the first-frame impression is an empty plain.
findings.notFixedAndWhy: Not fixed: moving the spawn, teleporting on claim, or shrinking the ring are three different design answers with different consequences for the depth tiers, and choosing between them is not an autonomous call.

unverified.label: screenshots are not persisted to disk
unverified.why: The Studio MCP bridge's screen_capture returns image data inline; it has no path argument, and store_image only reads FROM disk. So screens/*.png could not be written and screens[] carries assertions and verdicts but no file references. The images were inspected — they are evidence that was looked at, not evidence that was filed — and this rung's own rule is that an image without a written assertion is a way to feel verified, so the assertions are recorded here instead.

unverified.label: the live service singletons are unreachable from the MCP plugin thread
unverified.why: MEASURED: require(Server.services.salvage.SalvageService) from execute_luau returns a module whose _context is nil and _armed is empty, while the same services answer correctly over the wire. The plugin/command-bar context keeps its OWN module cache, so it cannot observe the running game's in-RAM state. Every server-authority assertion above was therefore taken over the real wire instead, which is a better probe anyway — but any future probe that wants in-RAM state must know this.

unverified.label: multi-client contention and cross-server persistence
unverified.why: Untestable by construction at this rung: one session cannot contend with itself, and game.JobId is "" in Studio, so SessionStore's Studio-GUID fallback is load-bearing rather than defensive.

unverified.label: T2.5 (the automated edit-mode playtest) never ran
unverified.why: The run-in-roblox lane cannot bind its hardcoded port 50312, which now falls inside Windows' dynamic reservation 50305-50404. See tests/engine-pass/ENGINE-FACTS.md (2026-08-08). This rung ran with the rung below it unrun, which is stated rather than glossed.

unverified.label: the density and horizon shots were not taken separately
unverified.why: The world has no dynamically spawned population to frame for density, and spawn-eye already answers horizon at this ClockTime - the sky is in frame and is the finding. Not attempted rather than attempted-and-passed.

screens.assertion: In Play mode with the default player camera, the HUD is actually on screen — a player sees a readout, not an empty viewport.
screens.observed: DeepReachHud present with 156 descendants and 8 top-level regions. Legible and populated: TOP DIVERS (#1 of 1, 452), SALVAGE 2.0/s with a smelter bar, DOME 1 'your dome . secured', SUPPLY DROP DAY 1 'next in 19h 48m', STRUCTURES with server-priced rows, DEPTH 1 x1, and the offline modal 'WHILE YOU WERE AWAY / +250 CREDITS / smelter filled at 250 after 8m — 255 lost, upgrade it'. The cap-loss line is the design's teaching moment rendering correctly.

screens.assertion: From above the world bounds, the trench is actually built — the dome plots and depth tiers occupy the space the config claims, not an empty baseplate.
screens.observed: Camera at (11.5, 1333, 0) looking at (11.5, -437.5, 0). The full ring of dome plots is visible with a 'YOUR DOME' billboard over the claimed one, against 145 non-character parts spanning 1856 x 1833 studs. This shot also independently confirmed the hud-panel-overflow finding: STORE and HIDE SHOP are drawn on top of the Hull Plating and Pearl Drone rows.

screens.assertion: After HudRoot clips its slots, no text from one slot is drawn over text from another — and the panels degrade by truncating rather than colliding.
screens.observed: Same viewport (1220x455), same session shape. The structures panel now ends cleanly at 'Smelter Tank . Lv 0' and the STORE / HIDE SHOP buttons sit fully legible below it; nothing is drawn over anything else. The cost is visible and accepted: TopRight's five status badges are clipped away entirely at this height. This is the shot that verified the fix, because the rect-based probe cannot see clipping.

screens.assertion: From the spawn pad at eye height, facing the way a player faces, there is something to see on frame 1 - not a void, not the inside of geometry.
screens.observed: Not a void, and not inside geometry - but a BRIGHT BLUE AFTERNOON SKY over a flat cyan baseplate, with the dome ring a thin line of grey blobs on the horizon ~917 studs away. For a game whose one-line pitch is an abyssal salvage tycoon this is the wrong scene entirely. See finding abyssal-scene-not-configured.

screens.assertion: At ground level beside a claimed dome, that region reads as what it is - a player standing at their plot can tell what they are looking at.
screens.observed: A translucent blue dome over a dark textured pad on a grey baseplate. Legible AS GREYBOX, which v1 declares it is, so this neither passes nor fails the intent: the shapes are placed and distinct, and there is nothing thematic to read. Recorded as cannot-tell rather than pass, because cannot-tell is not a pass.
